<!-- pr-reviewer: 66df3e5b46865fb6a9ae077ec23c6eebb2833898 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Review tier: SAFETY. This PR changes the posted G-code of the Tormach post (`assets/posts/tormach.cps`) and one NC golden.

### What looks good
- The change is small and has one guard. The post records the tool of its last `M6` (`loadedTool`). A consecutive request for the same tool skips the pre-change lift, `G30` and `M6`.
- The first tool change of a program is always written. `loadedTool` starts as `null`. The engine loads a new script context for each post run (`Script::load` in `engine::run_program_with`), so the value cannot go into a different program or a "one file per operation" program.
- A return to an earlier tool (T4, T7, T4) changes the tool again. Only one tool number is kept, not a set.
- The skipped path keeps the safety steps: the tool note, `G49` in the section line, then `G43 H<n>`, then `G53 G0 Z0` before the spindle start and before any X/Y or A move. `xyUnknown` stays `true`, so the clearance move `G0 Z<clearance>` comes before the first X/Y traverse.
- The A axis is safe. `endPreamble` sets `aNow = null` at each section end, so the next section always writes `G53 G0 Z0` and then `G0 A..` again, also without `G30`.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/1626-repeat-tool.md` records the public-document reading and the alternatives that were dropped. The PR does not rely on a same-tool `M6` exception in PathPilot, which is what the issue asked to check.
- The new test file has a provenance line and a Gate map. `expect` is only in tests. The file has 81 lines.
- The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1626`. The PR does not change snapshot PNGs, `PROCESS_VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, dependencies, `scripts/`, `.github/` or `build.rs`. It does not change `crates/ui`, so no screenshots are necessary.

### Golden check (line by line)
`docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`: the PR removes exactly three lines from the second T1 section (FLAT A90): `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T1 M6`. The lines that stay are correct:
- `M9` / `M5` end the first section at `Z0.875` (work). No motion occurs before the next lift.
- `G17 G90 G54 G40 G49 G80`, the tool note, `G43 H1`, `G53 G0 Z0` (Z to the top of travel), the belt note, `S6000 M3`, `M8`.
- `G53 G0 Z0` and then `G0 A90` - the index occurs at the top of travel.
- The section 2 motion lines are the same as before. The T2 section still writes `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30` / `T2 M6`.
- No other NC or CL golden moved. The `microarc_test_part` suite compares the golden exactly and passes.

### Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main `14aa3abd`, no conflicts)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: pass, 0 failed (10.0 min).
  - kernel: `step_agreement` 15 passed.
  - post: 20 suites, 143 passed, 0 failed (this includes `tormach_same_tool` 2/2, `script_tormach`, `tormach_traverse_clearance`, `probe_tormach`, `work_offset_index`).
  - app: 31 suites, 184 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored (this includes `microarc_test_part` 2/2, `tormach_toolchange_lift`, `tormach_safe_retract`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `between_setups`, `tormach_post`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass.

### Mutations (made by this reviewer in the local worktree, each one then restored)
| Mutation in `tormach.cps` | Result |
|---|---|
| Set `xyUnknown = true` only when a tool change occurs | killed: `repeated_tool_skips_...` fails (no restated traverse after the second `G43`) |
| Write the `liftZ()` after `G43` only when a tool change occurs | killed: `repeated_tool_skips_...` fails (`S1500 M3` follows `G43 H4`, not `G53 G0 Z0`) |
| Keep only the first loaded tool (`if (loadedTool === null) loadedTool = tNo;`) | killed: `a_different_tool_...` fails (T4 after T7 gets no `M6`, so T7 would cut with H4) |

After the restore, `git diff` of the file is empty and both pins pass again.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The commit type is `fix(post)`, but issue #1626 has the `enhancement` label. The merge lane follows the commit type. The maintainer can decide if this goes in now or at the cut.
2. After an `M0` setup change between two sections that use the same tool, the program now continues with no `G30` and no `M6`. This is correct if the operator does not change the tool at the stop. The decision file can mention this case in a later edit, if the maintainer wants that.
3. A PathPilot Hub run of a same-tool program was not done (the PR body says this). It is not necessary for this merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 66df3e5b46865fb6a9ae077ec23c6eebb2833898 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (one safety question, see "Requested before merge").

This is an independent review. The author's own review marker on this head is not used.

## What looks good
- The skip condition is one guard, `if (loadedTool !== tNo)` at `assets/posts/tormach.cps:441`. `loadedTool` starts as `null`, so the first tool of the program always gets G30 and M6.
- The post keeps `G43 H<n>`, the `G53 G0 Z0` lift and the clearance move before the first X/Y move in a skipped section. `xyUnknown = true` is now set in both branches.
- The `G49` line in the preamble still cancels the length offset before each `G43`, so no old offset stays active.
- A different tool, or a return to an earlier tool, changes again. `loadedTool` holds only the last M6.
- Spindle stop (`M5`) and restart (`S.. M3`) are still stated, as the golden shows.
- The decision file is complete. The commit subject and the `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1626` lines are correct. No process file and no snapshot PNG is touched. There is no new dependency.

## Cases where a tool change is skipped
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| First tool of the program | Not skipped (`loadedTool` is `null`). |
| Same tool number, next section, same setup | Skipped. G43, lift and clearance remain. Correct. |
| Same tool number, different setup or WCS | Skipped. `G54..G59`, `G49`, `G43 H` are stated again. Correct for a tool that stays in the spindle. |
| Different tool number | Changes. Pinned by the test. |
| A, B, A | Changes each time. Pinned by the test. |
| After an operator stop (`M0`/`M1`, setup change) | Skipped. See requested change 1. |
| After a probe cycle (`M0` "check probe result") | Skipped when the next section uses the same number. |
| Two different physical tools with the same number | Skipped. The post sees only the number. |

## Results merged with main (locally, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, trial merge of origin/main clean)
- `camcraft-post` suites: tormach_same_tool 2, script_tormach 11, tormach_traverse_clearance 4, probe_tormach 7, probe_spindle 2, probe_spindle_stop 2, first_traverse_clearance 9, comp 9, cycle_hop 7. All pass.
- `camcraft-app` suites: microarc_test_part 2, tormach_post 10, tormach_toolchange_lift 3, tormach_safe_retract 4, tormach_fourth_axis 12, between_setups 8, recorded_post_streams 5, program_entry 9, tool_after_state 5, probe_op 12, conformance 7, after_op 10, setup_mounts_post 8. All pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutation check: I changed the guard to `if (true)` (old behaviour). Both new tests FAILED. I changed it to `loadedTool !== tNo && tNo !== 7`. The test for a different tool FAILED and the repeat test passed. So the pins do detect a wrong skip. I restored the file.

## Goldens
Only `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc` changed. It loses exactly three lines before the second T1 section: `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T1 M6`. This is what the change explains. `G43 H1`, `G53 G0 Z0` and the spindle start stay. No other NC, CL or recorded post stream changed, and the suites above that read them pass.

## Requested before merge
1. Decide the operator-stop case, and state it in the decision file or in the post. After `M0`/`M1` (setup change, `MSG, SETUP CHANGE`, probe check) an operator may take the tool out of the spindle. The post now skips `T.. M6` for the same number, and the control cannot know the spindle is empty. G43 then applies the offset of a tool that is not loaded. Please either reset `loadedTool = null` after an emitted `M0`/`M1`, or add a pinning test and a written reason that this case is accepted. `afterOp()` is at `tormach.cps:493-515`.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Do two different tools with the same number exist in one program? I did not find a refusal for it in the post. If the app already refuses it, one sentence in the decision file closes the question.
- The tests use a synthetic stream (DRILL, tools 4 and 7). The real second-section case is covered only by the three-line golden change.

## Not exercised
No real PathPilot control, no Tormach simulator, no physical machine and no cutting ran. I did not run PathPilot's handling of M6 or G43. Windows-only and macOS arms were not run (no `cfg` change in the diff). The full quick gate plan, the ui suites and the release gate were not run. The suites listed above are the ones the diff and the tormach module touch.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 439e77ee8967deb107a00ed4680ac6ea2fff3405 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

The change that our review at 66df3e5 requested is in this head.

**Delta 66df3e5..439e77e**
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps:516` sets `loadedTool = null` after the M0 or M1 that `afterOp` writes. This covers a program stop, an optional stop and a setup-change stop.
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1043` does the same after the M0 of a probe-result check. We did not request this one. It is correct: the operator can reach the tool there too.
- I searched the post for other M0 or M1 writes. There are no more. M2 and M30 end the program.
- `crates/post/tests/tormach_stop_tool.rs` adds four pins. Each one posts the same tool twice with a stop between the sections. It checks that M6 is written again, preceded by `G53 G0 Z0` and `G30`, followed by G43 and the lift. The decision file records the reason and the rejected alternative.

**What looks good**
- The first tool change stays unconditional. A different tool, or a return to an earlier tool, still changes.
- Each section keeps G43, the Z lift and the clearance before its first X/Y move.
- The only golden change removes exactly three lines before the second T1 section in `microarc_test_part.nc`. It is explained in the body.
- No process files, no snapshot PNGs, no new dependency, no unwrap or panic in the post script.

**Results merged with main (fe1a94c), locally**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: tormach_same_tool 2, tormach_stop_tool 4, script_tormach 11, tormach_traverse_clearance 4, probe_tormach 7, probe_spindle_stop 2, recorded_streams 12, post_engine 33. All pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`: microarc_test_part 2, tormach_post 10, tormach_toolchange_lift 3, tormach_safe_retract 4, tormach_program_end 3, recorded_post_streams 5, after_op 10. All pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutation check 1: I removed the reset at line 516. Three pins fail (program stop, optional stop, setup change). The probe pin stays green, as expected.
- Mutation check 2: I removed the reset at line 1043. The probe pin fails. The three others stay green.
- I restored the file after each check. No golden or snapshot was regenerated.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Not exercised**
- No real control, no PathPilot Hub, no physical machine.
- Windows-only and macOS arms of the suites: the diff has no cfg(windows) or per-OS value. I ran the Windows build only.
- I did not run the UI suites, the other crates or the release gate. The diff does not touch them.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The optional stop (M1) is treated as a stop even when the control skips it. This is the conservative choice, and the decision file says so. The cost is one extra tool change.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
